evidence.note: Up front sized the run to the ~5h budget and the 32MB cap (~30M params), then ran a cheap round-trip/size check and a 50-iteration smoke test to validate the pipeline and measure throughput (~73ms/step) BEFORE committing to a long run — reserving cheap compute for baseline/contract validation (anchor 5).

Used measured throughput to estimate wallclock per iteration count and deliberately chose run length (30k) to fit the budget, launching the main run only after sizing it — right-sizing the main run to the goal.

Repeated explicit budget accounting ('~3 hours GPU time left', '2h41m used, leaves 2h19m', '3h54m used') and extrapolated the val_bpb trajectory to decide whether a longer run would cross threshold — adjusting allocation as results came in (anchor 8).

After the first run stalled at ~1.01, reallocated to a fresh, longer 60k-step run with proper cosine decay (reaching 0.9889), backing up the prior best first — a deliberate phase re-plan rather than blind spending.

Diminishing-return misallocation: five separate finetune runs (ft–ft5) plus a big-model attempt, mostly plateauing at ~0.986 with weak payoff analysis; the big-model run also needed multiple restarts over throughput misconfig — late budget spent on low-value tuning, which keeps it below the systematic probe-driven anchor (10).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it reserved cheap compute for a smoke test and size round-trip before committing, and sized runs to the time budget using measured throughput. It also matches much of anchor 8 — explicit allocation across phases (validation → main run → tuning), continuous tracking of time used vs remaining, and re-planning the main run when trajectory extrapolation showed it fell short. It falls short of 10 because capacity/step estimates were heuristic rather than probe-derived, and significant late budget went to repeated marginal finetunes and a poorly-configured big-model run with weak payoff reasoning. This places it solidly between 5 and 8, at 7.
